answer: A garden economy resists sybils by making trust grow slowly: newcomers may only tend small plots, and every completed job plants a public, peer-checked record in the shared garden. A fake identity starts as bare meadow with no history and must do real work to earn each plot, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand separate harvests. Like a raven circling overhead, a random auditor swoops in unannounced and demands live proof of one past job; an agent that cannot answer loses its plots and starts again from the meadow.
